newsitem.title: INDIA: No immediate threat to Indian government - Congress.
newsitem.headline: No immediate threat to Indian government - Congress.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Friday that the legal cases involving former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao posed no immediate threat to its support for the centre-left government.
Congress general secretary Devendra Dwivedi was asked if two cases in which Rao has been named had implications for the party's support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front government.
"I don't think there is any threat to the United Front government arising out of what has happened, immediately," Dwivedi told Reuters.
On Thursday, federal police filed charges against Rao in a forgery case and a judge denied the former prime minister legal protection against arrest in a criminal conspiracy case.
Indian stock markets fell on Friday on worries that Rao's legal problems could stir political uncertainty.

Rao stepped down as Congress chief last Saturday after a court upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court on September 30 in the criminal conspiracy case. He remains head of the Congress parliamentary party, which includes all deputies in the federal parliament.

Asked if he meant that there might subsequently be a threat from Congress to the United Front government, Dwivedi said: "No, I don't say that. We are talking of, so far as the stock market is concerned, stock market reaction on a day-to-day basis."
Dwivedi was asked if, over the longer term, the legal cases could affect Congress's relations with the United Front. "I don't see anything happening at the immediate time," he said.
Deve Gowda's minority coalition depends on Congress support in the lower house of parliament.
Earlier, Dwivedi told a news conference that there was no pressure on Rao to step down as head of the Congress parliamentary party.
